=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
Line or code reference: The per-cycle completion-status maintenance block (lines ~10300-10377) and the terminal-failure `continue` gate at line 9853, in interaction with the judge stall-cycle limit (line ~12649-12660), fingerprint-repeat cap (line ~13073-13091), and max-recovery exhaustion (line ~13099-13113) paths.
Problem: The per-cycle completion-status maintenance block runs at lines ~10300-10377, deriving `_completion_status_text` from wave-level signals (`ANY_FAILED`, `WAVE_COMPLETE`, `PROJECT_COMPLETE`) and calling `update_completion_status_comment`. It defaults to "in-progress". The terminal-failure paths in the judge section (stall-cycle limit, fingerprint-repeat cap, max-recovery exhaustion) all execute AFTER the maintenance block in the same loop iteration, setting `status="failed"` in the state file, posting separate one-shot failure comments, and calling `continue`. None of them call `update_completion_status_comment "failed"`. On the next poll cycle, line 9853 (`if [ "${PROJECT_STATUS}" = "failed" ] ... continue`) skips the completion-status block entirely because PROJECT_STATUS is now "failed". The same issue affects `mark_integration_branch_missing_failed` (line ~2585), which sets `status="failed"` but does not call `update_completion_status_comment "failed"`.
Why it fails at runtime: The pinned human-readable completion-status comment on the tracking issue permanently shows `State: in-progress` for a terminal-failed project. The operator reads this comment as the first-glance dashboard and will see an actively-running project when the project is in fact terminally failed. The V2 state comment and Telegram CRITICAL alerts correctly reflect failure, but the completion-status comment was explicitly designed to give the operator a quick status read — it must also reflect terminal failure. The `mark_validation_failed` function (which was extended in this last autofix run) correctly calls `update_completion_status_comment "failed"` in both the deterministic and exhausted-recovery paths, confirming the intent that terminal failures should update the pinned comment. The non-validation terminal failure paths were overlooked.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

Line: ~10297-10350 (completion-status maintenance block)
Problem: The `_completion_status_text` derivation logic defaults to "in-progress" when `ANY_FAILED` is not "true" and `PROJECT_COMPLETE` is not "true", without checking `PROJECT_STATUS` for terminal failure states.

- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
Line or code reference: Lines 10315-10327 (completion-status maintenance block, `_completion_status_text` derivation)
Problem: The `_completion_status_text` variable is derived exclusively from wave-level signals (`ANY_FAILED`, `WAVE_COMPLETE`, `PROJECT_COMPLETE`) and defaults to "in-progress". It does NOT check `PROJECT_STATUS` for terminal failure states. When a project transitions to "failed" via terminal failure paths that do not mark wave sub-issues (e.g., judge stall-cycle limit exceeded, repeated fingerprint cap reached, max recovery attempts exhausted, integration branch missing), `ANY_FAILED` remains false because no wave issue carries a failed label. The next poll cycle derives `_completion_status_text="in-progress"` and overwrites the "failed" status that the terminal failure path wrote to the pinned completion-status comment.
Why it fails at runtime: The pinned human-readable completion-status comment on the tracking issue misleads the operator, showing `State: in-progress` for a terminal-failed project. While the V2 state comment and Telegram CRITICAL alerts correctly reflect failure, the completion-status comment is designed as the operator's first-glance dashboard and should accurately reflect terminal failure states.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh

If the control flow nesting is incorrect, the force-merge safety gates (Gate A label check, Gate B audit health check) may execute in the wrong scope, potentially allowing unsafe force-merges or skipping valid recovery candidates.
